summary: A is materially closer to the frozen contract: it preserves Add unchanged, validates inputs, reuses multipartbody.NewFile, and keeps existing tests. B makes an explicitly forbidden behavioral change to Add and weakens its prior test coverage.
reasons: A preserves FilesService.Add’s signature and behavior, whereas B eagerly reads and buffers every caller-provided Add body, changing streaming, memory, timing, and reader-error semantics.
A explicitly rejects an empty filename and nil content before constructing a request; B has no visible validation for either condition.

A retains the existing Add test and adds Upload coverage. B replaces the existing Add test with one that no longer verifies the HTTP method, path, or full decoded response, contrary to the requirement not to weaken existing tests.

Both implementations reuse internal/multipartbody.NewFile and produce replayable Upload bodies, but B adds unnecessary duplicate machinery through a new private add method and broadens scope by changing Add and documenting that unrelated behavior change.
risks_a: Upload duplicates Add’s option handling, request execution, response decoding, and missing-data check instead of routing through Add as explicitly required.
The added tests do not visibly cover empty filename, nil content, or source-reader failures.
The retry test does not explicitly set RetryAllMethods: true, making its intent less clear for the reported POST-retry scenario.
risks_b: It violates the explicit requirement to preserve Add behavior by eagerly consuming and buffering arbitrary custom multipart bodies.
Upload routes through the new private add helper rather than the existing public Add method required by the contract.

Empty-filename and nil-content validation is not visible in Upload, and no validation or source-reader-error tests are added here; correctness would depend on undocumented helper behavior visible nowhere in the patch input materials provided to the judge.
